files: app/src/main/java/com/os73/dosos73/OutputStore.kt: preflight, space-check and UnknownSize recovery interactions
scope.method: Static baseline review using git show b89b957. Source working-tree changes were not reviewed as baseline, modified or reverted. No build, tests, emulator or publication was run. CommitRace06 is excluded.

findings.title: Space preflight counts already retained resume bytes as new allocation
conditions: A direct task has a valid incomplete ResumeJournal/checkpoint and its partial body is retained after pause/failure.
The origin accepts a matching 206 continuation, so only the remaining body must be allocated.
Available storage exceeds the remaining download plus publication copy and reserve, but is less than the complete analysis size multiplied by copies.
findings.evidence: Before invoking transfer(), baseline lines 46-50 pass task.analysis.sizeBytes and copies=2 for MediaStore or 1 for SAF into StoragePolicy.requireAvailable. This does not subtract the retained checkpoint offset. TransferProcessor lines 111-114 explicitly retain direct partial data on non-complete, non-user-cancelled outcomes. DirectDownloader lines 164-169 read the checkpoint, lines 190-206 validate a matching 206 and reuse prior.offset, and lines 221-223 preserve/seek to that offset. With a 1 GiB total, 768 MiB retained and 1.4 GiB available on the common cache/publication filesystem, 256 MiB remaining + 1 GiB publication + 32 MiB reserve fits, but the unconditional preflight requires 2 GiB + reserve and fails before the resumable downloader runs. For SAF on another filesystem, the equivalent cache example is 512 MiB available versus only 256 MiB remaining + reserve.
findings.impact: A paused or failed task can remain blocked with STORAGE_FULL despite sufficient space to finish its valid resume. The retained partial file itself contributes to the false refusal.
findings.recommendation: Make resume admission account for durable bytes already present, then check the actual response mode: matching 206 needs remaining bytes, while a 200/restart must be rechecked for a full replacement. Keep publication space separate and retain overflow-safe comparisons.
findings.verification_limit: Control-flow and arithmetic finding only. No device fixture was executed; the example assumes the existing checkpoint and origin response satisfy the downloader's validation.

findings.title: Recovered UnknownSize documents are indexed as zero-byte files
conditions: A nonempty SAF publication is recovered through OutputStore.recover.
The provider returns a readable pipe/descriptor with statSize=-1, as supported by the existing UnknownSize provider fixture.
findings.evidence: Baseline OutputStore lines 20-24 convert descriptor.statSize=-1 to 0 with coerceAtLeast(0), then pass 0 to LibraryRepository.remember. PublicationReceipt.recoverPlan already fingerprints the entire stream and compares its actual byte count with the receipt before returning (PublicationReceipt lines 87-90); the accurate expected byte count is durable in the receipt. LibraryRepository.remember persists the supplied bytes, and LibraryScreens line 125 displays item.bytes. RecoveryTestDocumentsProvider lines 62-67 deliberately returns a pipe for unknownSize=true, so this is a supported provider condition rather than an invalid empty file.
findings.impact: A successfully recovered nonempty document appears as 0 B in the saved library and leaves incorrect persistent size metadata.
findings.recommendation: Return the verified byte count from publication recovery, or otherwise reuse the verified receipt/fingerprint byte count when statSize is unknown. Do not map a negative size to a known empty size.
findings.verification_limit: Static finding only. Existing PublicationRecoveryTest lines 67-75 calls PublicationReceipt.recover directly, so it does not exercise OutputStore.recover's library indexing path.

test_gaps.gap: No storage admission test includes a retained partial/checkpoint. Add matching-206 cases that fit only after subtracting durable bytes, plus a 200 fallback case that must recheck full allocation. This covers finding 18-01.

The current Long.MAX_VALUE/copies=2 rejection is useful but there are no exact-boundary cases: available=reserve with bytes=0/null; available=reserve-1; bytes=(available-reserve)/copies and one byte above; copies=1 and a large copies value. No overflow defect was found for valid nonnegative inputs: the policy divides usable space instead of multiplying bytes.

OutputSafetyTest covers a successful exact-byte publication, while FailureClassifierTest only covers a direct IOException message containing ENOSPC. No inspected fault provider injects ENOSPC after partial writes, on flush or on close. Add a deterministic provider fixture asserting STORAGE_FULL when the cause is preserved, no published success, deletion of only the unverified temporary output, and recoverable receipt behavior if deletion also fails.

Only the outer exception message is classified. A wrapper with a generic outer message and an ENOSPC cause is not covered. Treat this as missing compatibility coverage here; no specific platform/provider wrapper was executed or proved in this review.

Existing coverage combines UnknownSize with rejected rename and checks only receipt recovery/non-deletion. Add normal successful OutputStore.save and OutputStore.recover paths for a pipe descriptor, assert exact content and nonzero indexed byte count, and inject a truncated pipe to verify fingerprint rejection. This covers finding 18-02.

test_gaps.area: Destination and cache on different volumes
test_gaps.gap: No fixture models cacheDir and MediaStore publication residing on distinct filesystems. The save-time StatFs query uses cacheDir, so device coverage should establish correct space admission for supported adopted/removable/primary-volume layouts. No concrete device failure is claimed.
